text:
Anthony Duclair has played for nine NHL teams, and in his second year on Long Island he's still doing what earned him all those chances: scoring a little more than his looks say he should. He has four goals on 2.3 expected and a 20% shooting percentage, including a one-timer to open the scoring against the Devils on Saturday. NHL Edge has his hardest shot in the top 5% of the league.

The problem is everything else. The Islanders have been much worse at five on five with him on the ice than without him, about nine points of expected goal share, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more against him last season than against all but 1% of forwards. That's a big price for a depth scorer.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him getting good shots off passes across the slot, which helps explain the finishing. But 20% won't hold. Our range has him at 12 to 23 goals over a full season. With injuries up front he'll keep getting minutes; the question is whether his goals outrun what the other team gets when he's out there.
headline: Duclair scores, and gives some back
